📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

Trump Could Order Another Strike on Iran as Midterm Elections Near


After several weeks of relative calm, the prospect of a new escalation between Washington and Tehran is once again moving to the forefront. 

According to reporting by The Atlantic, the Trump administration is considering several military strike options against Iranian targets, including the possibility of launching an operation before the November 3 midterm elections. 

No final decision has been made. U.S. officials cited in the reporting said the scope of any potential operation, its objectives and even whether it should go forward remain under discussion. Still, the fact that such scenarios are being actively prepared is significant. 

The White House is seeking to maintain pressure on Tehran while weighing the military, economic and political consequences of another confrontation. Energy prices are a particularly sensitive issue. A fresh escalation in the Middle East could drive up oil and gasoline prices in the United States, putting additional pressure on household budgets just as voters head toward the polls.

A new U.S. strike would also carry major military risks. An attack on Iran could trigger retaliation from Tehran and set off another cycle of violence across the region. American forces stationed throughout the Middle East could become targets, while U.S. facilities and interests could face retaliatory attacks.

The Strait of Hormuz represents another major vulnerability. Any disruption to shipping through the strategic waterway could have an immediate impact on global energy markets and intensify economic pressure on Western countries.The Pentagon is therefore working through multiple scenarios, but preparing military plans does not necessarily mean an attack has been authorized. 

The U.S. military routinely develops operational plans for a range of potential threats.The situation would change dramatically if Washington decided to significantly reinforce its military posture in the region and ordered the Pentagon to carry out one of the prepared options.

According to recent reports, the U.S. military command responsible for the Middle East is being instructed to remain prepared for the possibility of renewed large-scale operations against Iran. Potential targets could include Iranian military and energy infrastructure as well as facilities connected to the country’s nuclear program.

Diplomatically, the situation remains just as uncertain. Channels between Washington and Tehran have not completely closed, but negotiations remain extremely fragile. Iran says it is prepared to continue talks under certain conditions, while Washington continues to pursue a policy of maximum pressure.

Trump himself has kept his intentions deliberately ambiguous. The president has not ruled out another military operation while leaving the door open to a diplomatic agreement. The strategy allows the White House to keep pressure on Tehran without formally announcing another war.

The approaching midterm elections, however, add an explosive political dimension. A new military campaign could become a serious liability for Republicans if it led to sustained increases in energy prices, additional American casualties or a prolonged conflict. 

Conversely, a limited operation portrayed as swift and successful could allow Trump to reinforce his image as a tough leader and demonstrate that Washington still holds the initiative against Iran. That calculation is at the heart of growing speculation about a possible strike before the election. 

For now, there is no confirmation that a U.S. attack is imminent. No final order has been announced, and diplomatic options have not been exhausted. But the message from Washington is unmistakable: as the U.S. midterm elections approach, the possibility of another military confrontation with Iran is once again on the table.

🔔 South Korea targets November review for second stage crypto legislation 

🌐 South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has set November for a National Assembly subcommittee review of the Digital Asset Framework Act, rejecting claims that work on the country’s second stage crypto legislation has been delayed. According to Seo Na yoon, head of the FSC’s virtual asset division, the regulator and lawmakers are moving in the same direction on legislation covering digital asset issuance and distribution, including stablecoins. Speaking at a National Assembly seminar in Seoul on Sept. 22, Seo said differences remain over when the government will submit its draft, but the November review remains part of the planned timetable. 

⚡️ “The FSC is not dragging its feet at all. We share the same view,” Seo said, responding to criticism over the pace of the legislation. “The direction has already been set, and while detailed discussions may be necessary in the process, there is certainly no intention on the FSC’s part to delay.”

🔗 Seo said the regulator wants the legislation passed quickly and expects discussions to proceed using bills that lawmakers have already introduced alongside the government’s proposal. Ten digital asset and stablecoin bills are currently pending in the National Assembly, giving lawmakers existing proposals to work from before the government completes its version.
